extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, CRU staff, and practitioners handling inter partes reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidelines for USPTO examination of inter partes reexamination proceedings that are concurrent with federal litigation, including handling of court decisions, suspension/stay issues, examiner amendments, estoppel, and petitions to terminate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written communications requirement in merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: All communications between the Office and the patent owner (and the third party requester) which are directed to the merits of the merged proceeding must be in writing and filed with the Office for entry into the record of the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to merged reissue/inter partes reexamination proceedings to ensure the record reflects any substantive communications; oral communications on merits are not appropriate for the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: No interviews in merged reissue/inter partes reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews, both personal and telephone are not permitted in a merged reissue/inter partes reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accordingly, the examiner is not permitted to telephone the patent owner/reissue applicant and obtain authorization to make an amendment; all substantive communications must be written and entered into the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s amendments permitted only for formal matters (with Notice of Allowability)
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner’s amendment to deal with formal matters such as grammar, incorrect spelling, or incorrect number; i.e., matters that do not involve a rejection, do not go to the merits, and do not require the examiner to obtain approval. (Also: an examiner’s amendment to change the title.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a merged reissue/inter partes reexamination (as opposed to an application per se) all such examiner’s amendments must be made by formal examiner’s amendment accompanying the Notice of Allowability in order to provide notice of the changes made in the patent to both the patent owner/reissue applicant and the third party requester. See MPEP § 1302.04 et seq.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments that go to the merits cannot be made by examiner’s amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Note that any change going to the merits of the case (i.e., more than a formal matter) could not be made by examiner’s amendment accompanying the Notice of Allowability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A change going to the merits requires: (A) reopening of prosecution with the approval of the CRU Director, (B) an Office action suggesting the change to the patent owner/reissue applicant, (C) a formal amendment submitted by patent owner/reissue applicant, and (D) an opportunity for the third party requester to comment on the patent owner/applicant’s submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special dispatch requirement for inter partes reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise provided by the Director for good cause, all inter partes reexamination proceedings under this section, including any appeal to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences, shall be conducted with special dispatch within the Office. (35 U.S.C. 314)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statutory mandate requires expedited handling of inter partes reexamination unless the Director provides otherwise for good cause; this shapes timing and decisions about stays/suspensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited handling when litigation is stayed for reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a request for reexamination indicates that litigation is stayed for the purpose of reexamination, all aspects of the proceeding will be expedited to the extent possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office actions in these reexamination proceedings will normally set a one-month shortened statutory period for response (rather than the usual two months). Response periods may be extended only upon a strong showing of sufficient cause (see MPEP § 2665). Special dispatch often becomes important in coordinating reexamination and litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of federal court decisions known at time of determination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a federal court decision on the merits of a patent is known to the examiner at the time the determination on the request for inter partes reexamination is made, the existence of a final court decision does not necessarily preclude a question of patentability because the Office uses different standards of proof and claim interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may accord deference to factual findings made by the court, but the determination of whether a basis for reexamination exists will be made independently of the court’s decision. Non-final holdings of invalidity or unenforceability are not controlling; only a final holding after all appeals is controlling (see In re Zletz; In re Etter; In re Swanson).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's three-question test when requester was a party to litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: When the examiner is aware that the third party requester was a party to previous federal court litigation as to the patent, the examiner must determine: (1) Was the federal court decision adverse to the third party requester as to at least one claim of the patent? (2) Was the federal court decision a final decision, after all appeals? (3) Is the issue being raised in the reexamination request the same issue as was raised in the federal court during the civil action, or an issue that the third party requester could have raised in the federal court during the civil action?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If (1)-(3) are all yes for one or more (but not all) claims, those claims will not be treated and the examiner’s action will point out the claims not treated and the reason why. If (1) or (3) is no for all claims, examination proceeds without discussion of these considerations. If (1) and (3) are yes but (2) is no for a claim, examination proceeds using guidance for non-party situations, but the examiner’s action will discuss considerations (1)-(3). If the examiner later learns the decision is final and all three are yes for all claims, notify SPRS who will contact OPLA for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of a final holding of claim invalidity by a court
rubrics_metrics.description: A final holding of claim invalidity or unenforceability (after all appeals) is controlling on the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such cases, a substantial new question of patentability or reasonable likelihood of prevailing would not be present as to the claims held invalid or unenforceable. Where all claims for which reexamination was requested are affected, the reexamination will be vacated/terminated by the CRU Director. Use form paragraph 26.80 at the beginning of the Office action for claims held invalid by the court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to notify the Office of federal court decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 CFR 1.985(a), the patent owner in an inter partes reexamination proceeding must promptly notify the Office of any federal court decision involving the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt notification enables the Office to review whether a substantial new question of patentability or reasonable likelihood of prevailing remains and whether termination or other action is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for a grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.182 to terminate prosecution (pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 315(c)/317)
rubrics_metrics.description: A grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.182 to terminate prosecution of claims under reexamination must provide evidence that the following requirements, which track pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 315(c), have been satisfied: 1. The third party requester was a party to the litigation; 2. The decision is final, i.e., after all appeals; 3. The court decided that the requester/party had not sustained its burden of proving the invalidity of any claim in suit, which claim is also under reexamination; and 4. The issue(s) raised in the reexamination proceeding are the same issue(s) that were raised or could have been raised by the requester in the civil action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence should include a copy of the district court decision, any jury verdict, any CAFC decision including any mandate, any dismissal of an appeal by the CAFC, any Supreme Court ruling on certiorari, and submission of a copy of the district court’s docket is recommended. For item (1) show requester named in court documents; for (2) show finality (mandate, dismissal, docket); for (3) show which claims were before the court (verdict form, docket, other court documents); for (4) show the issues are the same or could have been raised (compare invalidity contentions, jury forms, trial materials).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence and standards for showing prior art 'availability' (newly discovered prior art exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: The statute does not prevent assertion of invalidity based on newly discovered prior art unavailable to the third-party requester and the Patent and Trademark Office at the time of the inter partes reexamination proceedings. Prior art was unavailable at the time if it was not known to the individuals who were involved in the civil action or inter partes reexamination proceeding on behalf of the third-party requester and the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To show a reference was 'available' the patent owner must provide evidence that the reference was known to the requester (actual knowledge) at a time when it could have been raised in the civil action (e.g., before trial). The petitioner may provide a discussion/comparison of prior art raised in reexamination vs prior art raised at trial, copies of jury verdict forms, defendant’s invalidity contentions, and docket entries to demonstrate availability or lack thereof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraph 26.80 when claims held invalid by court
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 26.80 Claims Held Invalid by Court, No Longer Being Reexamined — 'Claims [1] of the [2] patent are not being reexamined in view of the final decision of [3]. Claims [1] were held invalid by the [4].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner note: provide instructions for bracket insertions (which claims, patentee name, decision citation, and court name). Use this form paragraph at the beginning of an Office action when claims are no longer being reexamined due to final court invalidity holdings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment when requester was not a party to the litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: The issuance of a final court decision upholding validity during an inter partes reexamination, where the person who filed the request was not a party to the litigation, will have no binding effect on the examination of the reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office is not bound by a court’s decision upholding validity because district courts and the Office use different standards of proof ('clear and convincing' in court vs 'preponderance' in the Office) and different claim interpretation approaches. Deference will ordinarily be accorded to factual findings where evidence is the same, but the Office need not reach the same conclusion and may reject claims upheld by the court if sufficient reasons are present (see Ethicon v. Quigg; In re Swanson; In re Baxter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on considering suspension before reexamination ordered or with outstanding Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: A suspension will not be considered on its merits prior to ordering of reexamination. Also, suspension will not be considered on its merits when there is an outstanding Office action unless the patent owner: (1) provides a complete response to the outstanding Office action, and (2) includes a petition to suspend under 37 CFR 1.182.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until a proceeding exists to suspend, the Office must issue its decision on the request within the three-month statutory period. If a petition to suspend is to be considered on the merits while an Office action is outstanding, the patent owner must comply with the two requirements above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's authority to suspend inter partes reexamination for good cause
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 314 provides for special dispatch in inter partes reexamination 'Unless otherwise provided by the Director for good cause.' Accordingly, where there is good cause for the Director of the USPTO to suspend (stay) reexamination proceedings pending the conclusion of litigation, a suspension will be effected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such suspension is approached case-by-case; it will not be routine and will not be considered before reexamination is ordered. Ethicon limits indefinite suspensions for ex parte reexamination; for inter partes the Director may suspend if good cause is shown.
